title: Canonical derived module exchange and scalar restriction comparisons
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ be its pulled-back ring object [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, write $f^*$ for the exact module inverse image applied termwise to the ordinary unbounded derived category, and use its actual adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ with the K-injective total direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For composable $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$, denote by $c_{f,g}:(gf)^*\cong f^*g^*$ the canonical pullback-composition identification. For a commuting square $h:T\to X$, $q_Z:T\to Z$, $q:X\to U$, $s:Z\to U$ with $qh=sq_Z$, define the square comparison $q_Z^*s^*\cong h^*q^*$ by these composition identifications and the equality of composites. Define $\operatorname{Ex}:s^*Rq_*\to Rq_{Z,*}h^*$ to be the $q_Z$-adjunct of that comparison followed by $h^*$ of the actual $q$-counit. No cartesianness or invertibility is required in this definition.
For a morphism $c:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of commutative condensed rings, let $\operatorname{Res}_{c,X}$ be exact restriction of internal scalars, applied termwise [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Its pullback comparison is the canonical $\operatorname{Res}_{c,X}f_{\Lambda'}^*\cong f_\Lambda^*\operatorname{Res}_{c,Y}$. Define the directional direct-image comparison $\operatorname{Res}_{c,Y}Rf_{\Lambda',*}\to Rf_{\Lambda,*}\operatorname{Res}_{c,X}$ as its adjunction mate. For a module $M$, the degree-zero scalar unit is the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction unit $M\to\operatorname{Res}_{c,X}(\Lambda'_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}M)$ embedded in degree zero and followed by the single-complex/restriction identification. In the normed extension $E\to\Omega$, use the actual postcomposition morphism $C_E\to C_\Omega$ on all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring].
